analysis:
In April-May 2019 Shah repeatedly set out a sequence: the Citizenship Amendment Bill first, then an NRC. BOOM records the sequence in his remarks at a press conference (23 April), a rally in Birbhum (22 April), an ABP News interview (2 Oct) and a rally in Hooghly (1 May). On 20 November 2019 he told the Rajya Sabha that an NRC would be carried out across the country (reported by Scroll, The Wire and Deccan Herald).

After the CAA was passed and protests followed, Modi said on 22 December 2019 at Ramlila Maidan that there had been no discussion of a nationwide NRC since 2014. BOOM found that claim inconsistent with earlier statements. On 24 December Shah told ANI there had been no discussion in cabinet or Parliament.

MHA written replies in the Lok Sabha on 4 February 2020 and 30 November 2021 state that no decision has been taken to prepare a nationwide NRC. No nationwide NRC has been conducted. The plan was therefore stated, then not implemented, without a formal announcement that it was dropped.

The verdict reflects the stated plan not materialising rather than a ruling on the later statements; the two positions (April and November 2019 versus the later government line) are both on the record.
